Where it began

Kagiso Rabada was born in Johannesburg on 25 May 1995. He first caught the eye at the 2014 Under-19 World Cup, which South Africa won. He took 14 wickets in the tournament, conceding barely three an over, and his six for 25 against Australia A were its best figures.

The Lions brought him straight into their first-class side. In February 2015, aged 19, he took 14 for 105 in a match against the Dolphins, including nine for 33 in the second innings, the best match return of the franchise era in South Africa.

The player

He arrived in international cricket at a gallop. On his one-day debut, against Bangladesh in July 2015, he took a hat-trick and finished with six for 16. His Test debut followed that November against India, and at Centurion in 2016 he took 13 for 144 against England, the youngest South African to take ten in a Test. By January 2018 he was ranked the top bowler in the world in both Tests and one-day internationals, aged 22, and that July he became the youngest man to reach 150 Test wickets.

By November 2026 he had played 75 Tests and taken 350 wickets at 22.11, with 17 five-wicket hauls, four ten-wicket matches and a best of seven for 112. That placed him 29th among all Test bowlers. He passed 300 in October 2024 and was part of the side that won the 2023–25 World Test Championship.

What made him special

Speed, and a habit of striking often. Few bowlers in Test history have needed fewer balls for each wicket, and in 2018 he took 52, more than anyone else that year. In 2022 he took five in an innings at Lord's, which put his name on the honours board there.

The bat was a more casual friend. By November 2026 he had made 1,104 Test runs at 12.13, with a single fifty and a best of 71. A Test hundred had not yet come his way by then, though nobody in the South African dressing room was complaining about the trade.

Away from the middle

He became the first player to win six awards at one Cricket South Africa dinner in 2016, then did it again in 2018, when he was Cricketer of the Year for the second time. That August, Wisden picked him as the finest young cricketer anywhere. In the IPL he was the leading wicket-taker in 2020, and in April 2023 he became the quickest bowler, by matches, to reach 100 wickets in the competition.

Away from cricket, in 2020 he and Cameron Scott set up a film company, Kingdom Kome Productions, and their first piece of work was The Ring of Beasts, a short film.

And finally

In 2016 he turned down an IPL contract to spend part of the summer with Kent, learning to bowl in English conditions. It looked a patient choice for a young fast bowler in a hurry. The honours board at Lord's suggests it paid off.
